outcomes: Execution facts leave the native engine while work runs, followed by the original persisted terminal session
A failed or canceled graph retains its actual verdict while a reporting outage leaves replayable state
A log reporter receives the same live event stream through its own selector and credential, independently of the session reporter
nonGoals: Interpreting CI policy, owning source-hosting credentials, or updating provider checks
Reporting admission, pre-execution failure or executor loss as fabricated task results
Establishing repository/provider provenance, same-principal isolation, or a metadata/network sandbox

requirements.text: Each selected capability (session-reporter, log-reporter) subscribes to the session event stream on its own and receives canonical persisted events during execution. Reporting finalizes on success, failure and cancellation. session.json closes before the session reporter's events final marker; the log reporter gets events.jsonl only. Graph verdict behavior stays authoritative. Each capability records its own subscribers.json entry; one capability's failure changes no other, no artifact and no verdict.

A cursor per capability retains provider identity, per-artifact sequence and offset, and at most one exact pending chunk before transmission. A successful acknowledgement binds the entire chunk identity; a lost acknowledgement replays the same bytes. sessions replay requires an exact finalized session id, replays only selected capabilities not yet delivered and rewrites only their entries, uses fresh credentials, and runs no workload DAG or lifecycle hooks.

The authoritative CLI captures and removes every capability's selection and token before extension setup, hooks and repository tasks. Only the capability's own provider process receives its token: never a task, a hook or the other capability's provider. A hosted run passes none; the protocol carries the run credential. Provider stderr and arbitrary error payloads are not echoed. Selection does not establish trust in a repository manifest/runtime, nor prevent same-UID, file, metadata or network access.

Limit chunks to 64 KiB, response lines to 96 KiB, RPCs to 5 s and 3 attempts. Live chunks wait for a full frame or 10 s (session reporter) or 2 s (log reporter). Each drain/replay stops 30 s after the last ACK or 5 min after it starts, naming the limit; cancellation caps it to 2 s without changing the verdict. Checkpoint reads stop at 192 KiB, replayed session.json at 16 MiB. Pending records take priority in sessions.keep; the oldest inactive expire with a diagnostic. Active locks permit temporary excess.
